problem: Current VLA models for embodied navigation are effectively stateless, processing each observation as if new, so they lack persistent spatial memory for long-horizon reasoning in VLN-CE. Flat recurrent or attention baselines struggle with long-horizon dependencies.
motivation: Long instruction-following navigation over hundreds of steps needs remembered rooms and landmarks. Human navigation uses a hierarchical internal model (objects, furniture, rooms) and attends mainly to changes, which suggests a multi-scale memory with adaptive computation.
key_idea: Use a three-level (Object, Furniture, Room) input-selective S4D state-space memory with learned Adaptive Computation Time halting, fused with language via a cross-modal decoder and trained with a stabilized DAgger pipeline.
insight: Removing the SSM memory drops SR from 15.0% to 1.0% on val_seen, and removing any single hierarchy level also hurts, with Furniture (-13.0 SR) and Object (-11.5 SR) most critical. Oracle Stop raises SR to 37.0%, so termination is the main bottleneck. The agent does better with the instruction removed (22.0% vs 15.0% SR), so language grounding was not achieved and the model relies on geometric priors. Absolute performance is very low, and the val_unseen SR of 1.5% shows little generalization.
method: Perception encoders: frozen DINOv2-Small (last layer trainable) on RGB plus a small depth CNN give 256-d visual features; frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B with mean-pooling gives a 768-d language embedding.

Hierarchical S4D memory: three levels (Object d=256, Furniture d=384, Room d=512), each an S4D kernel (N=16) with input-dependent step size Δt in [0.001,0.1], an input gate, and cross-attention to adjacent levels' context; output uses mean-pooling over state rather than C.

Adaptive Computation Time: a learned halting gate per level, up to M=5 shared cycles with sequential gating (Furniture blocked until Object halts, Room until Furniture halts) and a guaranteed fallback update. The ponder cost is computed but not added to the loss.
Skip fusion: the three level states are concatenated into a 1152-d spatial state.

Cross-modal VLA decoder: bidirectional cross-attention between spatial and language features, then a 4-layer causal Transformer decoder over 4 actions. ALiBi and RoPE are defined but not active in the forward path.

Stabilized DAgger: oracle shortest-path data, BC warmup for 20 epochs, then DAgger with β decaying from 1.0 to 0.7, a 20k FIFO replay buffer with per-class caps, inverse-frequency class weights, adaptive entropy bonus (0.05–0.15), down-weighting of spinning or stuck segments, and three-tier collapse detection that resets β.

setting.backbone: DINOv2-Small (frozen except last layer) + Qwen2.5-1.5B (frozen) + trained hierarchical S4D memory and Transformer decoder
setting.training_data: R2R-VLN-CE train (~14k instructions, 61 scenes) with oracle shortest-path-follower actions for BC warmup and DAgger rollouts; no extra data. The DAgger rollouts were drawn from the val dataset, so there is potential contamination.
setting.action_space: low-level discrete FORWARD 0.25 m / LEFT 15° / RIGHT 15° / STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time (the oracle expert is used only in training; the Oracle Stop diagnostic uses GT goal distance)

numbers.extra: single seed; DAgger rollouts drawn from the val dataset (possible contamination)

numbers_note: All results use 200-episode subsets and a single seed. The other rows (No Memory, No Room/Furniture/Object, Oracle Stop, modality-dropout v5e14) are ablations or diagnostics and are not listed here.
results: The full model gets 15.0% SR on val_seen and 1.5% on val_unseen, far below the ~40% SR the paper cites for published methods. Removing memory drops it to 1.0%/0.0%. Oracle Stop reaches 37.0%/10.0%, and No Language beats the full model (22.0%/6.0%).
limitations: Very low absolute performance with a 90% relative SR drop on unseen scenes, and no comparison to published baselines
DAgger rollouts were drawn from the val dataset, so results may be contaminated; single seed and 200 episodes
ALiBi/RoPE and the ponder loss are not active in the implementation, and language grounding was not achieved (the agent does better without language)
compares_to: CMA (cross-modal attention baseline; cited only, not evaluated)
internal ablations (No Memory, No Room/Furniture/Object, No Language, No Vision, Oracle Stop)
